data.title: bn-33l3: scope the zero-alloc counter to the measuring thread
data.description:
MECHANISM (named, reproduced, not inferred): libtest post-spawn harness bookkeeping observed by a process-global allocation counter.

nextest DOES process-isolate this suite (argv is 'alloc-HASH --exact NAME --nocapture', one test per process), so cross-test pollution was never possible — but process isolation is not THREAD isolation. nextest does not pass --test-threads=1, so libtest runs at concurrency greater than 1 and executes the test body on a SPAWNED thread (library/test/src/lib.rs:461) while its harness main thread stays alive in the same process. /proc/self/task shows exactly 2 live threads.

That harness thread allocates AFTER spawning us: lib.rs:462 running_tests.insert (first HashMap insert) and lib.rs:463 timeout_queue.push_back (first VecDeque push). Measured margin from the harness's last allocation to this test body's first instruction: 20-100us on an idle host (n=200, min 20.5us, p50 45.2us). A preemption in that gap puts those allocations inside the measured window, and the old process-global static ALLOCS booked them against the hot path.

Caught live under stress-ng (cpu 40, vm 8x1G, hdd 4) plus concurrent mess-log suite runs: an instrumented twin reported 'phase1 encode delta=1' with the allocating thread reported as name=main and a backtrace ending at test/src/lib.rs:462, landing 5.3ms inside the phase-1 window. Second instance of the same class, also captured: at TEST_WARN_TIMEOUT_S (60s) the harness thread allocates 3 more times for the slow-test notice (lib.rs:409/416/472).

FIX: count into a const-initialised, destructor-free thread-local Cell<usize>; assert on the measuring thread's delta. The process-wide count is kept but never asserted on, only reported in failure messages.

TEETH (all verified): Part 0 canary fails if the counter silently stops counting; a new guard runs a helper thread churning 1000 allocations across an open window and asserts this thread's delta is 0; mutation tests — one Vec::push per encoded batch fails (19999 counted), disabling the thread-local fails the canary, reverting to the process-global counter fails BOTH tests with the original signature.

VERIFICATION: 700 runs of both tests concurrently in-process (harsher than nextest isolation) under the reproducing pressure profile: 0 failures. 307/307 mess-log, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean, cargo +nightly fmt --all --check clean. Statistical limit stated honestly in the bone comment.

Scope: crates/mess-log/tests/alloc.rs only. No hot-path production code touched — the hot path does not allocate; the harness did.
